title: Kubernetes RBAC Abuse
overview: Review a Kubernetes audit record for an unexpected grant of cluster-wide administrative access.
prerequisites: Be comfortable reading timestamps and kubernetes audit projection fields.

attack.name: Additional Container Cluster Roles
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: An interactive actor granting cluster-admin through a ClusterRoleBinding needs immediate authorization review.
evidence: Check the request actor, role reference, subject and API response. Review later activity by the new subject.
false_positive: An approved bootstrap or break-glass action can grant high privileges temporarily.
tuning: Allow vetted controller identities and track expiration of temporary bindings. Audit edits as a separate behavior.
response: Preserve audit events and revoke the confirmed unauthorized binding. Inventory later access by the subject.
prevention: Use least-privilege RBAC, change review for privileged bindings, and admission controls where appropriate.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: Fields summarize a Kubernetes audit event. The lab neither connects to a cluster nor mutates roles.

questions.prompt: Why is this binding high impact?
options: ClusterRoleBinding and cluster-admin grant broad privileges
It sorts first in the list
questions.explanation: Both binding scope and referenced role matter for effective access.

questions.prompt: Who may use the new permissions?
options: Only the actor who submitted the request
The subject named in the binding
questions.explanation: The actor performs the grant. The subject receives access.
